newsitem.title: USA: Virginia jobless rate falls to 3.8 pct in November.
newsitem.headline: Virginia jobless rate falls to 3.8 pct in November.

text.p: Virginia's unemployment rate dropped to 3.8 percent in November from 4.1 percent in October, the state Employment Commission said Thursday.
The rate was the lowest for November in seven years, but equaled the March and April rates for this year.
"The rate has been good all year and it generally gets lower in the fall," said William Mezger, senior economist at the commission.
In the Richmond-Petersburg area, the jobless rate dipped to 3.3 percent in November from 3.7 percent in October.
Statewide, the employment rate was boosted by school hiring and the holiday retail season.

Government employment increased by 6,800 people to 609,200 in November, while tourism saw a seasonal decline of 3,700 to total 916,300. Construction jobs decreased by 1,000 to 175,000 but that was still the highest November level in seven years.
